label: Source cuts across admitted input records
term: source cut across admitted input records
definition: For one fixed Exercise dictionary, effect event e and source bearer c, SourceCut means every admitted record for exactly e has at least one contributor event borne by c. AvailableRecord separately requires admission, the same effect token, at least one contributor, and occurrence of every contributor and enabler at the selected scenario. PopulatedCut is their conjunction. SourceInactive excludes occurrence of every contributor of c in all admitted records; RecordCovered separately requires every allowed occurrence of e to have an AvailableRecord. These are record/input semantics, not a definition of productive receipt, exercise, existence of a bearer, or either sourced PRESERVATION sense.
note: Analyst reconstruction; attribution deferred. Reuses DEF-JOINT-CAUSAL-GROUPS and DEF-JOINT-SCENARIO-SUFFICIENCY rather than replacing their semantics. Admission, contributor/enabler classification, bearer assignment, occurrence and allowed scenarios are inherited primitives with OPEN application obligations. Exercise remains distinct from available inputs. The two-alternative circuit and uncovered control certify only the stated record semantics; no transitivity, asymmetry, well-foundedness, causal direction or withdrawal possibility is inferred. SourceCut can be vacuous without a record; PopulatedCut excludes that case. It is sufficient for the stated cut consequence, not necessary for dependence: an admitted but impossible alternative can make it fail. The same effect token fixes the numerical target event; identifying that event as this same bearer's esse, rather than its illumination/operation, remains OPEN. The effect's bearer is m.bearer e; source distinctness is not automatic. Complete proposed outcome, consumer coverage, positive role/coverage burdens and next tests: docs/eternity-dependence-connection.md, Atemporal source-cut component (2026-11-17). Original sense declarations and allowances remain unchanged.
